observed_vs_expected: The experimental trajectory partially aligns with expectations but fails to sustain the predicted improvement. The first expectation anticipated consistent improved edge steepness and stable tightest_margin; however, the best_target_score peaked at 0.3793961408114576 in round 2 before collapsing to 0.2931312227391984 in round 3, indicating volatile rather than improved steepness. The tightest_margin remained at 0.1944395410436397, showing no marked stabilization. The third expectation regarding three distinct half-wave cavity layers is not yet evidenced, as the optimizer dispersed thicknesses across a broad 31–80 nm range without forming clearly grouped resonant bands.
deviation_mechanism: Multi-cavity distributed Bragg reflectors operate on strict constructive interference; the resonant condition demands precise round-trip phase accumulation per cavity. When layer thicknesses drift by only a few nanometers away from their nominal optical thicknesses, the accumulated phase error causes destructive interference, rapidly degrading cavity finesse and flattening the transmission edge. The abrupt score drop from round 2 to round 3 coincides with substantial thickness perturbations in the central stack (e.g., layers 11–13 shifting between 70.71 nm and 77.81 nm across runs). Without tightened initialization bounds or phase regularization, the optimizer wanders out of the narrow resonant basin, converting a physically viable topology into a numerically unstable search.
continue_rationale: Only one round (round 3) has been executed since the historical peak (round 2). The prescribed stop condition requires two consecutive rounds of improvement less than 1e-3 relative to the historical best, which has not yet materialized. Additionally, valid_candidates remains robust at 9, well above the threshold of 3 that would trigger topology reduction. The physics demonstrates boundary sensitivity rather than fundamental infeasibility, warranting continued exploration with adjusted parameter constraints.
insight_for_next: Constrain thickness initialization to ±8 nm around nominal quarter-wave/half-wave optical thicknesses for the target wavelength band. Introduce a soft penalty on the variance of adjacent high-index layer thicknesses to suppress spurious phase modulation, and reduce the learning rate by 50% to dampen overshoot near the resonant basin boundaries.
insight_grounding: Round 2 score_history entry reached 0.3793961408114576, with candidate layers 11, 12, and 13 measuring 77.81479252840411, 75.84636135560402, and 72.93187321980072 nm, respectively. In round 3, the score_history entry fell to 0.2931312227391984, and the corresponding layers drifted to 76.87571916924408, 70.71320045428818, and 74.06476484274141 nm. The ~5 nm phase shift in layer 12 directly precedes the collapse, confirming that bounding initialization within ±8 nm of the round 2 proven dimensions will preserve the resonant condition while preventing further drift.
